answer: A garden of agent identities stays honest when each new identity costs more than the last: the first account posts a small refundable bond, the second posts double, the third four times as much, and so on. A single honest agent keeps one cheap walnut-sized stake, while an attacker planting a thousand fake identities must lock up a fortune before earning anything. Bonds are returned after a clean history, but proven fraud forfeits the stake, so the fable of free infinite identities collapses under real, escalating cost.
